body.statement: Extend the bounded-width compiler to every \(2\le p<q\) and every same-transitive-closure pair \((G,G')\). Decide whether \(G'\in\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\setminus\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\) over every legal positive-real factor-line branch in each full-dimensional sign and variance chamber \(C\subset\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{branch},p,q}(G,G')\). Prove soundness, completeness, and termination without unrestricted real quantifier elimination. On acceptance return a finite chamberwise dense positive-real realization cover; on rejection return a checkable full-dimensional linkage, affine, covariance-cone-face, or positivity separator. Give a closed-form bit-operation and coefficient-growth bound in \(p\), \(q\), \(B\), and the realized branch-interaction structure, and derive infinite equality and generic-strictness families. The theorem-specific locus may exclude \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)=0\); candidate twins may be variance-neutral, both signs of each true variance change must be covered, and no pointwise claim is made on the excluded hyperplanes.
body.justification: This is the unresolved theorem-level frontier: a graph-specific positive-real decision principle for all noninjective soft-LCD systems.
body.gap: Problem 5.2 motivates covariance-versus-higher-cumulant strictness for the published source model. The class \(\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\) is instead a robust generic-chamber refinement internal to \(\mathcal M_{p,q}\); convex, birational, and half-trek results do not yield its all-graph projection completeness.
body.consumer: The companion LCD workflow can use acceptance certificates to report genuine covariance alternatives and rejection certificates to justify when higher cumulants remove them.

obligation.what_is_open: Give a graph-specific, non-quantifier-elimination criterion deciding density of the projection of the complete union of legal positive-real covariance branches in every full-dimensional true chamber, together with realization or separator certificates and uniform complexity.
obligation.obstruction: The finite branch representation does not control projection of a union: alternate loading lines, nonunique positive baseline decompositions, support hyperplanes, and Schur-positivity regions can meet after elimination.  A successful rational branch or nonsingular local Jacobian proves only local interior, while failure of one branch is not a separator for their union.  The frozen core contains no invariant proving that these interactions are localized for arbitrary graph pairs, and the supplied draft explicitly records this all-graph projection-completeness step as open.
obligation.attempted: Reduced general regular twins to \(\mathfrak B_p(G,G')\), derived the fork's eight bivariate systems, and verified the rational collision against the original five covariance equations.  The remaining classification would require eliminating the candidate variables uniformly over all true parameters; the available route is unrestricted real quantifier elimination, which does not satisfy the question's non-QE requirement.
obligation.partial_result: Every regular covariance twin is represented by the finite family \(\mathfrak B_p(G,G')\), so unrestricted real-algebraic projection would decide each fixed graph pair.  The terminal part already has linkage and affine certificates, and the four-node fork has an exact eight-branch reduction to bivariate rational sign systems with an explicit positive collision.  What remains is a uniform non-quantifier-elimination argument proving that the union of all positive branches has dense projection, or producing a full-dimensional separator, in every true sign-and-variance chamber.
